description: We are USTPeeps, a multidisciplinary team from the University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines – Cagayan de Oro (USTP-CDO). Bringing together individuals from the fields of Data Science, Computer Science, and Computer Engineering, we combine our skills in data analytics, technology, and innovation to build BlueShift and explore how data can help address real-world environmental and socioeconomic challenges.
summary:
BlueShift is an interactive Earth-observation and fisheries analytics platform that investigates how changing ocean conditions are associated with fisheries production across the Philippines.

The platform integrates NASA Aqua MODIS satellite observations, including sea-surface temperature (SST) and chlorophyll-a concentration, with fisheries production statistics from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). By combining environmental and fisheries data across geographic locations and time periods, BlueShift allows users to monitor ocean conditions, track local fisheries production, and explore potential relationships between them.

Through interactive visualizations, geographic exploration, correlation analysis, and lagged comparisons, users can investigate environmental trends alongside changes in fisheries production.

Initially focusing on Mindanao, BlueShift aims to make Earth observation data more accessible and actionable for researchers, fisheries managers, and policymakers. By connecting satellite observations with local fisheries statistics, the project encourages data-driven understanding of marine ecosystems and supports informed decisions toward more resilient fishing communities.
details:
BlueShift brings together satellite-derived ocean observations and Philippine fisheries statistics into one interactive analytics platform. It helps users investigate how changes in ocean temperature and productivity are associated with changes in local fisheries production.

The platform has four main components:

1. Ocean Monitor

Uses NASA Aqua MODIS satellite observations to visualize and explore:

  • Sea-surface temperature (SST).
  • Chlorophyll-a concentration, an indicator of ocean productivity.
  • Spatial distributions and temporal trends of ocean conditions.

2. Fisheries Tracker

Uses Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) fisheries statistics to explore:

  • Fisheries production measured in metric tons.
  • Production by region, province, and species.
  • Annual and quarterly production trends.
  • Top-producing species and geographic comparisons.

3. Ocean-Fisheries Relationship Explorer

Connects environmental observations with fisheries production to investigate potential relationships. Users can:

  • Select a province, species, and environmental variable.
  • Compare ocean conditions and fisheries production over time.
  • Examine Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients.
  • Explore scatterplots, trend lines, and statistical summaries.
  • Investigate potential lagged relationships between environmental changes and fisheries production.

4. Regional Insights

Provides an interactive geographic view of Mindanao, allowing users to compare environmental conditions and fisheries production across provinces and identify notable spatial and temporal patterns.

How Does It Work?

BlueShift integrates three major data sources:

  • NASA Earth Observation Data: Aqua MODIS Level-3 products provide monthly chlorophyll-a and sea-surface temperature observations at approximately 4 km spatial resolution.
  • Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA): Fisheries production statistics provide quarterly records categorized by species and geographic location.
  • Geographic Data: Philippine administrative boundaries from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX) provide geographic references for spatial analysis and visualization.

The datasets undergo data acquisition, cleaning, preprocessing, geographic association, and temporal alignment. Satellite observations are aggregated to compatible geographic and temporal units to enable comparisons with fisheries production records.

Statistical methods, including Pearson and Spearman correlation, are used to explore relationships between environmental variables and fisheries production. Lagged comparisons further allow users to investigate whether environmental changes may be associated with production changes in subsequent periods.

Importantly, these analyses identify exploratory statistical associations rather than establishing direct causal relationships.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The Philippines relies heavily on fisheries for food security, livelihoods, and economic activity. However, environmental observations and fisheries statistics are often accessed and analyzed separately.

BlueShift addresses this gap by bringing these datasets together in an accessible platform.

Its potential benefits include:

  • For researchers: Provides an integrated environment for investigating relationships between ocean conditions and fisheries production.
  • For fisheries managers: Helps identify regional and temporal patterns that may warrant further investigation.
  • For policymakers: Makes environmental and fisheries information easier to explore and communicate.
  • For local fishing communities: Encourages greater awareness of changing ocean conditions and their potential implications for fisheries.

The initial study area is Mindanao, providing a foundation for exploring regional patterns before potentially expanding to other Philippine fishing regions.

Tools and Technologies

The project combines Earth observation data processing, statistical analysis, geospatial data integration, and interactive data visualization.

Key resources and technologies include:

  • Python: Data acquisition, cleaning, preprocessing, statistical analysis, and data integration.
  • Jupyter Notebook: Reproducible data processing and exploratory analysis workflows.
  • Next.js: Application layer powering the interactive web platform and user interface.
  • NASA Earthdata Cloud: Access to Aqua MODIS Level-3 chlorophyll-a observations.
  • NASA PO.DAAC: Access to Aqua MODIS Level-3 sea-surface temperature observations.
  • PSA OpenSTAT: Official Philippine fisheries production statistics.
  • Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX): Philippine administrative boundary datasets.
  • Statistical Methods: Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation, trend analysis, and lagged comparisons.
  • Geospatial Analysis: Geographic aggregation, spatial association, and regional comparisons.

What Makes It Different?

BlueShift transforms the idea of being an Earth System Trend Detective into an interactive data exploration experience.

Rather than examining satellite observations and fisheries statistics independently, it connects large-scale environmental changes with local production patterns. Users can move from observing ocean conditions to investigating fisheries trends and exploring possible relationships between the two.

Its combination of satellite observations, official national statistics, geographic analysis, and interactive statistical exploration provides a more connected perspective on the relationship between Earth's changing ocean systems and human activities.

Factors Considered

During development, the team considered:

  • Data compatibility: Ensuring satellite observations and fisheries statistics can be compared across compatible geographic and temporal units.
  • Spatial resolution: Accounting for the approximately 4 km resolution of the satellite products and the geographic boundaries used in the analysis.
  • Temporal alignment: Reconciling monthly satellite observations with quarterly fisheries production records.
  • Data quality: Handling missing observations, invalid measurements, and inconsistencies during preprocessing.
  • Statistical limitations: Recognizing that correlation does not establish causation and that fisheries production is influenced by other ecological, economic, and human factors.
  • Accessibility: Presenting complex environmental and statistical information through understandable visualizations and interactive exploration.

Our Vision

Better understanding of our oceans. Stronger local fisheries. More resilient fishing communities.

BlueShift aims to empower people to become Earth System Trend Detectives by connecting environmental observations with real-world fisheries data, turning complex datasets into insights that can support informed decision-making.
